page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Catchword "fuit" at the lower right and gathering mark "p" at the lower left, both below the last line.

main_text.p: iudicaturos Israelem contumacem: tamen Deo parendum esse, statuit.
main_text.head: DESCRIPTIO CIVI-tatis Ninivch.
main_text.p: Quanta fuerit amplitudo ciuitatis Ni-niueh, docet αὐξήσεως[?] Hebraeis familiaris, qua diuina quaedam eius magnitudo celebratur. Erat, inquit Propheta noster, Ni-niueh ciuitas magna Elohim, Deo. Ita in Psal. 104.16. Saturantur arbores Iehouae: cedri Libani quas plantauit. Additur per ἐπιξηγήσεως[?] itinere trium dierum: id quod nonnulli de uicinis pagis, ius comune ciuitatis obtinentibus, alij de ambitu urbis, alij deniq; de urbis regionibus praecipuis interpretantur.
Fuerunt sane quarundam urbium ambitus prodigiosae propemodum magnitudinis: ut exempla[?], quae subijcia[?], monent.
Carthaginis, cū eā deleret Scipio Iunior, ambitus fuit sex miliariū Germanicorum: diameter circiter duorū miliarium.
Constantinopoleos, cum eam Turcae, Anno Christi 1453, expugnarent, ambitus erat cētum & undecim stadiorum, id est, miliariū Germanicorū trium & dimidij.

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. Greek words marked [?] are uncertain. The page number "115" is hard to read at the top right. "exempla" and "subijcia" are doubtful readings. The line "Celebratur magnitudo Ecbatanę, quę" is continued on the next page by "fuit", the catchword. Printed hyphens at line ends were kept ("CIVI-", "Ni-"), and "Germanico-rum" was written whole because no hyphen is visible.
